Jordan / procurement team — Rachel from Redwood billing here. Quick notes on billing paths and what we typically see: 

1) AWS Marketplace Private Offer (recommended)
- Pros: consolidated invoice to your AP, AWS handles settlement with Redwood, faster vendor setup in many cases.
- Cons: requires marketplace onboarding for the paying entity and a completed W-9 or local tax form for invoicing.

2) Direct PO to Redwood (fallback)
- Pros: simple contract flow if you already have a supplier record for Redwood.
- Cons: some enterprise AP teams take longer to set up new suppliers; payment terms may vary.

Action items we need from Novus to prepare the private offer:
- Completed W-9 or local tax form (I attached Novus_W9_Request.form as a fillable stub).
- Billing contact name and email for AP (who receives invoices).
- Legal entity exact phrasing and tax ID to place on invoices.
- Any PO number format constraints (e.g., max length, prefix).

Tax & invoicing note: If the invoice must be issued to a specific subsidiary, we can place that legal entity on the invoice produced by AWS Marketplace, but the marketplace requires the paying account to be set up correctly in AWS beforehand.

Timing: to meet your fiscal close and our provisioning timeline, we recommend finalizing these items by June 24 so we can create the private offer and route through AWS for signature before June 30. If procurement needs more time, let us know and we’ll adjust the MAP.

I can join the Monday 6/15 sync to walk AP through what the invoice will look like.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
